title: Making and Running an Acrylamide Protein Gel
author: Robert Hooftman
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7syhnfw

steps.title: Prepare Spacer Plate
steps.instruction: Set up a spacer plate (0.75 mm, 1 mm, or 1.5 mm) with a cover plate in a clamp.

substeps.instruction: Check for leakages using water and ethanol.
Pour off ethanol and water and remove traces using filter paper.

steps.title: Prepare Separation Gel
steps.instruction: Prepare 10 ml of separation gel solution in a small tube.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 μl of 100x APS and mix by inverting the tube a few times.
Add 10 μl of 1000X TEMED and mix by inverting or pipetting up and down.

steps.title: Cast Separation Gel
steps.instruction: Pipette the separation gel between the glass plates until approximately 2 cm below the top of the cover plate.

substeps.instruction: Add isopropanol on top of the gel to remove bubbles and prevent drying.
Wait approximately 30 minutes for the gel to completely polymerize.
Pour off isopropanol and remove remaining residue using H2O.
Remove H2O traces using filter paper.

steps.title: Prepare Stacking Gel
steps.instruction: Prepare 10 ml of 4% stacking gel by adding the following ingredients in order: 6.1 ml dH2O, 1.3 ml Acrylamide (30%, 37.5:1; Bio-Rad), 2.5 ml Tris-HCl (0.5 M, pH 6.8), and 100 μl SDS.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 5 ml of the prepared stacking gel into a tube.
Add 50 μl of 100x APS and mix by inverting the tube a few times.
Add 5 μl of 1000X TEMED and mix by inverting or pipetting up and down.

steps.title: Cast Stacking Gel
steps.instruction: Pipet the stacking gel on top of the polymerized separation gel.

substeps.instruction: Insert a comb (corresponding to the gap between glass plates) to create either 10 or 15 wells.
Wait until the stacking gel is completely polymerized.

steps.title: Assemble Electrophoresis Cell
steps.instruction: Remove the plates from the clamps and place them in a casket with another gel or a buffer dam to generate a compartment.

substeps.instruction: Place the casket with the gel into a vertical electrophoresis cell.
Prepare 1L SDS-PAGE running buffer by mixing 14.4 g Glycine, 3.02 g Tris, 1 g SDS, and 0.9 L dH2O (or dilute 100 ml of 10x stock to 1 L).
Fill the casket to the top with SDS-PAGE running buffer and wait a few minutes to ensure there are no leaks.

steps.title: Load Samples
steps.instruction: Remove the combs from the gel and load samples along with a protein ladder.

substeps.instruction: For 15-well (small) gels: load approximately 10 μl (max 15 μl) per sample.
For 10-well (big) gels: load approximately 25 μl (max 35 μl) per sample.

steps.title: Run Electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Fill the electrophoresis cell with running buffer to the line for the corresponding number of gels (e.g., fill to the 2-gel line for 1 gel, or 4-gel line for 3 gels), overflowing the casket to ensure it is completely filled.

substeps.instruction: Put on the lid and set the power supply to 40V.
Increase the current to 120V once the samples enter the separation gel.
Turn off the current once samples have travelled far enough through the gel.

steps.title: Recover and Wash Gel
steps.instruction: Remove the casket, discard or reuse the running buffer, and open the glass plates to remove the gel.

substeps.instruction: Place the gel in a large petri dish.
Wash 5 times with water while gently shaking, or incubate for 30 minutes on a rocking shaker.

steps.title: Stain and Destain Gel
steps.instruction: Pour off the water and add Coomassie Blue staining.

substeps.instruction: Stain for 1 hour (or overnight) on a rocking shaker.
Pour off the staining solution (save for reuse) and add dH2O to destain.
Change the dH2O approximately every 60-90 minutes while on a rocking shaker.

steps.title: Visualize Gel
steps.instruction: Once destained, use a gel imager with a white screen and a Coomassie Blue visualization protocol to save and print the image.
